query: Crumbs {You're three floors up in the library with a paper bag of ginger biscuits from the village, which is against every rule painted on the stairs. Somewhere in the stacks the head librarian is doing her rounds, and her rounds make no sound at all.|Biscuits again, and the head librarian again, somewhere in the shelves. Footnote has smelt the ginger and is watching you from the next desk with enormous patience.|The bag rustles. Two stacks away, a floorboard doesn't.} Put the bag away and work hungry {You fold the bag into your satchel and work on an empty stomach. You get a great deal done, all of it about food.|The bag goes away. Your stomach complains loudly enough to echo down the stacks.|You work hungry. When the head librarian passes, she nods at your empty desk, as if she knows exactly what's in the satchel.} Eat them and risk it {You eat the whole bag a crumb at a time. Nobody comes. It's the best chapter you've ever read.|You and Footnote share the bag, one for you, one for the cat. The rounds pass two stacks away and keep going.|You eat them all and brush the crumbs into your sleeve. Nobody ever knows except the cat, who is not telling.} {The head librarian is behind you, holding out her hand for the bag. She takes it without a word. You hear her eating them, later, at the desk.|A crunch, and the lamp is suddenly at the end of your row. Your name goes in a book with a black cover.|Footnote knocks the bag off the desk at the worst possible moment. The head librarian arrives as the biscuits finish rolling.} See her coming {You glimpse the lamp turning into your row a breath before it does, and when it arrives there is nothing on your desk but notes and a very innocent face.|A moment ahead, every time. The bag goes under the book, the book comes out of the bag, and the head librarian passes and never knows.|You see her coming, and seeing her coming, offer her a biscuit. She looks at you for a long time. Then she takes one.}
